transcript: Some people could have ankle deep water in their yard. UT San Antonio says the phone warning can come after that. So its researchers built a flood station. It charges itself from light and needs no cell tower. Four optical sensors at different heights watch the water. A small chip on the station runs the AI itself. So it judges flood risk without a central server. Its radio signal can carry more than a half mile in streets. In open country, up to five miles to a hub. At the hub, a second larger AI maps flood paths for responders. The university reports early chip AI validation. Accuracy was 98.82%. The announcement reports no field result. It names no town with an installed station. Deployment is still the goal.
